newsitem.title: USA: Florida inmate to examine suspect electric chair.
newsitem.headline: Florida inmate to examine suspect electric chair.

text.p: A death row inmate will be allowed to examine the state's electric chair, which in March sent flames shooting from the head of a condemned killer, the Florida Supreme Court ruled Friday.

In a unanimous decision, Florida's highest court said lawyers for convicted murderer Leo Jones should have the opportunity to look over the chair, known as "Old Sparky," and interview witnesses to the March 25 execution of Pedro Medina.

It was Medina's fiery death that prompted the high court last month to suspend executions in Florida until at least September pending review of the electric chair to determine if it is working properly or should be turned off for good.

The high court postponed the execution of Jones, convicted for the 1981 killing of a Jacksonville policeman, until at least Sept. 15. In the meantime, it ordered that additional testimony be allowed to determine if the chair is working properly or if in its present condition it constitutes cruel and unusual punishment.

State experts brought in to investigate the chair after Medina's death blamed officials for not properly saturating a sponge used in the execution helmet. The sponge, they concluded, caught fire and sent 12-inch flames shooting from his head, filling the execution chamber with an acrid smoke and the smell of burning flesh.

Under the ruling Friday, Jones can call his own experts to examine all the equipment used in Medina's execution and will be able to interview witnesses to the execution, a group that includes a half dozen reporters. Oral arguments before the Supreme Court were scheduled for Sept. 15.
